title: Assignment 16 · Performance in good faith
summary: Performance in good faith. Assigned readings and principal cases for this class.
notes:
Dalton v. Educational Testing Service: ETS had to consider the relevant information it promised to consider, but the remedy was a good-faith reconsideration of the score rather than automatic certification of its validity.

Northwest, Inc. v. Ginsberg: The Airline Deregulation Act preempted this Minnesota implied-covenant claim because the obligation it sought to enforce was imposed by state law rather than voluntarily undertaken by the airline.

Market Street Associates v. Frey: Deliberately exploiting a contractual partner’s oversight could violate good faith, but the relevant state of mind could not be decided against the tenant on this summary-judgment record.

Bloor v. Falstaff Brewing Corp.: Falstaff’s best-efforts promise required attention to Ballantine’s sales volume; concentrating on Falstaff’s overall profits while allowing that volume to collapse did not satisfy the agreement.

Ng Giap Hon v. Westcomb Securities Pte Ltd and Others: The Singapore Court of Appeal declined to imply the proposed general good-faith duty into an agency agreement, while distinguishing that issue from narrower terms implied from a particular bargain.

Additional assigned materials: Bloor agreement paragraphs 1, 2(a), 8(a); Restatement of Consumer Contracts § 4.
